page.layout: Running head at top, centred: "IVRISCONSVLTVS" with page number 93 at the right. One column of running text, with a catchword "cu-" at the lower right.

main_text.p: versatos, ut minimè vererer illud ipsum affirmare mea sponte, quod postea cognoui à Fabio diserte traditū con-firmatumque fuisse: totam illam disputationem puerile esse, & à Cicerone in libris posterioribus abiectam contemptamque fuisse. quod vel cuiuis mediocri iudicio prudentiaque prædito facile intellectu est: cum præsertim tam sæpe partes pro genere numerentur. Quinetiam Fabiū ipsum in libro tertio & quarto, ubi tractatum hunc omnem controuersiarū explicat, plerisque illorum erroribus implicatum esse, facilè cu-

page.notes: Running head ornamental middle letters are hard to read; reading "IVRISCONSVLTVS" is a best guess. Long s is shown as f in the scan and is transcribed as s. Hyphens at line ends are kept only where they are printed; "cu-" is the catchword. Some words such as "versatos" and "uererer" are read from the scan; the first word "versatos" is a fragment continued from the previous page.
